title: Chapter 689
paragraphs: Chapter 689
Episode 176. Destiny for Two (3)
"It wasn't that I didn't, I couldn't."
"You seemed to have enough power."
"Chiron didn't merely express it, he genuinely didn't categorize me as a human. How could a non-human become a knight?"
"It seems like it would be no trouble for my father to hold onto you and educate you to become a human."
"Do you really think your father is the type to put effort into taming someone, let alone a beast?"
"I see. If my father didn't capture you himself, the Black Knights wouldn't have tried to persuade you further."

"I didn't particularly want to be a subordinate of Chiron. Rather, I simply desired to reach the realm he had reached, and the stimulation given by the Black Knights was the greatest. From then on, attacking Chiron and his knights became the most important part of my daily life. But it was often the case that I was mundanely suppressed by many, not one on one."
"Even if they don't capture you, there's no need to be harsh on an opponent they don't want to kill. According to your description, hmm, even cute...."
"And whenever I was suppressed, I always had a meal with the Black Knights at their camp. Even if I tried to run away, they caught me, bound me, and forced me to eat."
"Even to that extent? Was there a command to eat together whenever you encountered them?"
-"If you're going to kill, kill. What is this nonsense?"
-"It's the Lord's order. Make him eat."
"That's what they said."
At that point, Jin fell into a brief contemplation.
He was curious as to why Chiron had issued such an order.
For some reason, he wanted to figure it out himself rather than hear it from Hedo.
"Sharing a meal... he might have thought it a good way for you to acquire humanity. Also, it seems he believed it helped the Black Knights' mentality. The Black Sea is a dreadful land after all."
"I think so too, 12th flagbearer. It was something possible because I was a beast."
Though the two didn't know, Hedo had played a role similar to Ozdok who was currently part of the expeditionary force.
Hedo had spent such moments with Chiron's knights for quite a long time.
Eating together, blankly sitting by the campfire before leaving.
Sometimes they would have conversations, sometimes Hedo would be suppressed even while eating, and sometimes the knights would give Hedo advice on the sword.
They were becoming something like friends.
"Ah, it seems fitting that you would have simply become Runcandel at that time. How on earth did you fall into Ziplo and come this long way around?"
"Because it was not fate."
At first, it seemed that before long, Hedo would blend in with the Black Knights.
Both Hedo and the Black Knights thought so.
But it was just for a while.

"I was a beast, and Chiron and his knights were human. However, we were all becoming monsters in the end. My desire to resemble Chiron's sword was also gradually blurring. Madness was surpassing motivation."
While the Black Knights were confronting the Black Sea, Hedo was becoming weak from an inexplicable increasing madness.
The same was true for Chiron. The unique charm of Genesis was constantly isolating him from others, and the meals that they used to have quite convivially were gradually reduced in frequency.
Chiron's command certainly helped those who were withering, but it was merely a reprieve.
"The Black Sea is where you cannot survive without abandoning humanity, and Genesis is the place where you cannot control it without stepping out of being a human."
Timing, place. The meeting of Hedo and Runcandel was not good in all respects.
With no one leading, from the moment they stopped eating together, Hedo and the knights drew their swords only to kill each other again.

"That's how I, the Black Knights, and Chiron became middle-aged. Every time we met, we could see the traces of time that were faintly visible on each other's faces. It was like looking in a mirror. They must have felt the same looking at me."
The past of Chiron's Runcandel and Hedo was longer and gloomier than Jin thought.
"And I was thinking of challenging Chiron for the last time."
".....Looking at the flow of the story, it wasn't due to fighting spirit or competitiveness."

"That's right. I was thinking of dying. As I learned humiliation and revenge through Vanessa, I knew for the first time what it meant to be empty at that age. It was always filling me. I just didn't know."
Hedo's gaze remained fixed on the sky.
That void was the cause of Hedo's madness.
"As soon as I realized, the impulse that there was no more reason to live rushed in like madness. Investigating the sword, the past days that were just about survival were meaningless."
While the knights had a clear goal and loyalty even as they were becoming monsters, hence no reason to give up on life, it was not so for Hedo.
He was truly a man who had nothing.

"I met Chiron again and drew my sword. Until then, even if I aimed my sword at Chiron, other knights would confront me, but no one came forward. Instead, Chiron drew Barisada. Like the time when he silently cut down past challengers."
Hedo's skills at that time were only a few moves behind compared to now.
Despite having honed his skills in the Black Sea for decades, and with the advice and frequent confrontations with the Black Knights, it was thanks to his explosive progress from that point.
However, the fight didn't even come to fruition.
Chiron, the wall that he still cannot surpass today, had already been perfected at that time.
"When I came to my senses in the middle of the fight, Sir Chiron was looking down at me, who had collapsed. 'Kill me,' I said, what do you think Sir Chiron replied to me?"
Jin tried to imagine what Chiron would have thought.
Since nothing came to mind, he just gave the answer he would have given in the same situation.
"He might have asked why you didn't think of leaving the Black Sea."
At that, Hedo's eyes widened.
"Indeed...... you're like my son."
-Why are you still staying in the Black Sea?

"Thinking about it, it was a question I'd never heard before despite having spent so long in combat. The Black Knights never asked me that either. It's the same reason you don't ask a wild animal why it lives where it does."
In other words, it wasn't until then that Chiron tried to see Hedo not as a beast, but as a human.
-Go and live a human life. Stop chasing us.

"When I heard that...... I felt like I was going mad. I begged him several times to just kill me instead. My shattered body wouldn't respond to my attempts to stop Sir Chiron and the knights, who were calmly leaving. They had things to do, and I didn't."
Hedo lay on the spot for three days.
He couldn't move, but he hoped that as usual, the monsters would attack and devour him.
However, just as animals avoid the scent of predators, the monsters didn't dare approach because of the energy of Chiron that remained nearby. They didn't even twitch until Hedo got up again.

"And then I went out. I was exiled from the Black Sea by Sir Chiron. I didn't know the way back, but I just walked aimlessly and was already among people. I was never attacked by monsters on that road, it even made me think that those creatures were following Sir Chiron's will."
The world he returned to as a middle-aged man after leaving at fifteen was, for Hedo, no different from hell.
Because he had nowhere to go.
"Twelfth flagbearer, I always called the Black Sea my refuge."
"That's right."

"People can't grow in a refuge. When I came back to the people, there was no difference from when I was fifteen and left for the Black Sea. I had become a warrior close to tenth rank, but my inner self was still similar to when I killed the orphanage director."
The same situation continued as before he went to the Black Sea.
The only difference was that there was no one who underestimated Hedo and rashly attacked him.

His stature was similar to now, with the appearance of a lunatic with messy hair and a huge sword, coupled with his unique vacant yet gloomy energy, so he was not entangled in the squabbles of criminals.
Furthermore, except for a few times when Hedo lost his way, he did not seek out places where there were people.
He mostly spent his time blankly in mountains, seas, or deserted places.
"Did you not think of seeking the Garden of Swords?"
"Because I was an outcast. I guess you've never had that experience."
Jin remembered that before his regression, he was merely an outcast until he met Valeria after being exiled from his family.

"That's possible. So then...... around that time, Zephyr probably found you first. The tower master said he had been looking after Sandra since she was very young. That's the only possibility in terms of timing."
"That's true. Suddenly, Baekya came to find me when I was on an uninhabited island."
"Why did Baekya look for you?"

"It seems there were some Zephyr among the unfortunate challengers I killed in the Black Sea. One of the survivors who returned to the clan informed them of my existence. They were just waiting for me to get out of the Black Sea."
From the start, even if it wasn't Hedo, Zephyr always had people stationed near the Black Sea.
That way, they could confirm the Rune Kendels coming in and out of the Black Sea.
It was inevitable that Hedo caught their eye as he ventured into the human world, and subsequently was pursued.
Hedo, who had been starving for several days, easily swept Baekya away.
However, he could do nothing about the Wraith squads who subsequently ambushed him.

"Instead of dying, I was imprisoned. I thought that if I just stayed quiet, they would stop trying to persuade me and eventually kill me, but I was already in a state of being dead, with only my body alive. So all the conditions that the clan offered me were meaningless."
Of course, Zephyr did not kill Hedo until the very end.
Losing a few Baekyas was a small price to pay if they could gain a superhuman without a clan.
Furthermore, Zephyr was already researching mind manipulation at that time.
If Hedo was not ultimately captured, they could use him after the mind manipulation magic had been developed.
Hedo didn't know about such plans, but even if he did, he wouldn't have acted differently.
"How did Sandra move your heart when you were in such a state?"
At that, Hedo turned around and leaned on the railing, looking over at Sandra beyond the dining room.
She was laughing even more heartily than before, as if she found something very enjoyable.
